title: Just-in-time weight onboarding and passive KV rehearsal for cold-start mitigation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Reduce tail latency and token-cost overhead for cold starts on Dedicated fleets by introducing a just-in-time weight onboarding flow and a passive KV rehearsal subsystem that exercises model KV shapes without blocking live requests.
background: Dedicated fleets currently experience high p99 cold-starts when tenant traffic is routed to a node missing model weights or KV residency. Existing warm-pool strategies are effective but incur cost when scaling to many tenants or models. We need a hybrid approach that minimizes both latency and resource residency cost by loading model weights in a staged, non-blocking manner and pre-warming KV cache entries through low-cost rehearsal probes that do not affect tenant quotas or SLOs.
proposed_solution: 1) Just-in-time weight onboarding: when scheduler plans to route traffic to a node that does not have required weights, enqueue a prioritized background onboarding job that fetches quantized weight shards and applies a two-phase activation: a lightweight kernel mapping phase (enables warm start for short sequences) followed by full weight residency for high-throughput lanes.
proposed_solution_2: 2) Passive KV rehearsal: a tenant-scoped rehearsal agent periodically issues low-cost inference probes (single-token, synthetic prompts derived from tenant prompt signatures) that populate KV caches and validator fingerprints. Rehearsal respects tenant privacy (synthetic inputs, no logs), admission budgets, and provides a signal for capacity planner to prefer nodes with recent rehearsal activity.
proposed_solution_3: 3) Cold-window eviction watermark: introduce a short-term watermark per node that delays eviction of newly-onboarded weights for X minutes unless memory pressure requires immediate reclamation. This reduces churn for short re-routes and bursty tenants.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end cold-start latency reduced by >=30% for typical tenant workloads compared to baseline
Median token-cost increase for maintaining soft-residency watermark <= 3%
Rehearsal probes do not increase tenant billing or affect rate limits
No regression on steady-state throughput (throughput within +/-5% of baseline)
Automated canary shows safe rollback path and no data leakage from rehearsal probes
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind fleet config 'jit_onboard_v1' and 'kv_rehearsal_v1'. 2) Start with internal canary on low-traffic Dedicated pools for 48 hours. 3) Expand to 10% of production fleets with telemetry collection for 7 days. 4) Full opt-in stage with default off for new tenants. 5) After metrics pass, enable by default for fleets under 'throughput-optimized' profile.
success_metrics: P99 cold-start latency, resident-weight churn rate (loads/hour), rehearsal hit-rate (percent of routed requests with reused KV), additional memory footprint, tenant-reported errors, and cost delta per 1000 requests.
risks_mitigations: Rehearsal could accidentally hit tenant data: use synthetic, non-identifying prompts and strict scrubbers
Background onboarding may compete with serving traffic: throttle background jobs with priority-aware IO windows and circuit-breakers
Increased memory residency: implement soft-residency watermark and eviction scoring to bound budget
Incorrect rehearsal signals could bias routing: maintain conservative thresholds and require corroborating metrics before making routing decisions
test_plan: Unit tests for onboarding state machine; integration tests simulating rapid tenant bursts; chaos test where nodes are killed during onboarding; performance bench comparing cold-starts with and without rehearsal; privacy audit to validate synthetic prompt generation; load test to assert no regression in throughput.
engineering_notes: Leverage existing weight-streamer interface (streamed quant shards) but add a two-phase activate API: map_only -> map_and_lock
KV rehearsal agent runs on fleet control plane and uses a separate low-priority token bucket for admission
Expose per-tenant rehearsal budget in Console and telemetry to allow customers to opt-out
Instrumentation: add tags 'jit_onboard=true' and 'kv_rehearsal=true' to traces for aggregation
Fallback: if onboarding fails or exceeds time budget, fallback to a compatible smaller model variant per routing policy
open_questions: What is the default soft-residency timeout (5/10/15 minutes)?
How to synthesize rehearsal prompts for narrow-domain tenants without leaking structure of customer prompts?
Should rehearsal footprint be charged as a platform cost or absorbed by tenant quota?
Tuning for multi-tenant nodes with mixed priority customers: how to weight rehearsal signals
